text_summary.body: When the wall had no breaches left but the doors were not yet hung, Sanballat and Geshem four times invited Nehemiah to meet in the plain of Ono; Sanballat then sent an open letter alleging, on Gashmu's word, that the Jews planned rebellion and that Nehemiah wanted to be king, with prophets to proclaim him; Shemaiah, hired by Tobiah and Sanballat, urged him to shut himself in the temple; Nehemiah refused and asked God to remember Tobiah, Sanballat and the prophetess Noadiah.

setting.body: An accusation of rebellion to the Persian court was a serious threat (cf. Ezra 4:12–16).

terminology.gloss: A dialect form of Geshem (Ryle; Keil).

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik notes that only priests could enter the temple building, so Shemaiah's advice was a trap (cf. Uzziah).

open_questions: The extra-biblical attestation of a Geshem/Gashmu of Qedar was not researched in this unit.
